document.title: Talking Points for PC 0930 on 14 September 2001
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Unspecified] Powell's talking points for an NSC Principals Committee meeting on the immediate response to 9/11. Objectives: setting the stage for a forceful response, eradicating bin Laden's al-Qaida, and eliminating safehaven for terrorism. Powell notes moderate Arabs are seeing terrorism in a new light, which is key to the coalition.

key_claims: The US campaign aims to eradicate Usama bin-Laden's al-Qaida and to hold accountable those who harbor or support the 9/11 attackers.
On 13 September 2001 Armitage secured Pakistan's agreement, via ISI chief Mahmud, to cooperate operationally with the US.
The State Department prepared a consensus recommendation not to suspend humanitarian aid, especially food, to Afghanistan, though no decision was made.
India and Egypt pledged unprecedented support through US ambassadors Blackwill and Welch.
State sought broader coalition support via NATO, OIC, G-8 and Central Asian and Caucasus states.
